reading.body:
Greg Landsman's AI record is dominated by data centers and electricity costs, not by AI safety or model regulation.

Of the 17 events, at least seven are bills whose subject is data center siting, data center tax treatment, or the power load data centers place on the grid. The No Secrets for Data Centers Act, the Protecting Communities from Data Center Impacts Act, the No Harm Data Centers Act, the Reverse Big Ugly Tax Breaks for Data Centers Act, the SHIELD Act on large load electricity demand, and the Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act all sit in that cluster. A separate cluster concerns AI in health care, including the Doctors Not AI Act, the Ban AI Denials in Medicare Act, and a resolution on a CMS pilot using AI to determine Medicare coverage. Only the AI for Secure Networks Act and the Critical Infrastructure AI Cyber Defense Pilot Program address AI in the security and infrastructure sense.

The dates run from April 2025 to September 2026, and the data center and energy bills are concentrated in the later part of that window. That is consistent with the grid and power supply becoming the live political problem around AI rather than the technology itself. For AI scaling, this is the constraint showing up in legislation: if data centers face siting limits, local impact requirements, or new electricity cost rules, the buildings and the power behind compute get harder to build, and compute is what every AI capability depends on.

What the data does not show is whether any of these bills became law, what their text actually requires, or how Landsman voted on the ones he did not sponsor. It records one $1,000 contribution from Meta Platforms' PAC and no other money, so it cannot support any claim about who funds him. It also draws no link between the contribution and any bill, and the page states that placement in date order is not a claim of causation.

summary: Every dated AI event this site holds for Greg Landsman: bills sponsored or cosponsored, recorded votes on AI bills, and money from AI company and AI-focused political committees, newest first. 17 events.
